## Welcome to Edgeware 
Edgeware is a collectively governed public network and project incubator. 

It is owned, operated and secured by EDG holders who work together to steward the entire economic, organisational and cultural resources of the project through open, meritocratic and democratic processes that are all executed on-chain on the project's own blockchain.

It is the second oldest mainnet chain in the Substrate ecosystem - younger than [Kusama](https://kusama.network), but older than [Polkadot](https://polkadot.network) with over [10M blocks finalised.](https://edgeware.app/#/explorer) 

## No ICO or fundraising event
The project was bootstrapped using a [lockdrop](https://medium.com/commonwealth-labs/whats-in-a-lockdrop-194218a180ca), where holders of ETH could lock their tokens for 3, 6, 9 or 12 months in return for receiving EDG.
It was also possible for smart contracts holding ETH to signal on behalf of their holdings, enabling [Binance](Binance announcement), Coinbase and [Aragon](https://github.com/aragon/AGPs/blob/master/AGPs/AGP-35.md) to receive distributions on behalf of their users.
The total ETH locked in the process finalised at 1,199,728 ETH, with signaled funds (from smart contracts) at 4,346,544 ETH with over 4000 different Edgeware addresses created in the lockdrop process, from over 10,000 transactions.

Binance finally distributed the tokens in March 2022, creating a massive long-tail of EDG holders.
## Wide and fair distribution
With over 90% of the token distributed to the public in the lockdrop, the door was opened to a community of holders who could mediate the decision making powers of the founding team Commonwealth Labs. 

Edgeware was originally positioned as a platform for _incubating governance experiments_, in the end the broad distribution has ensured Edgeware is itself the primary experiment.
